source.title: A treatment-resistant default mode subnetwork in major depression.

confidence_rationale: The single most on-target paper for Q-061: after 12 weeks of antidepressant treatment the POSTERIOR DMN subnetwork hyperconnectivity normalised, but the ANTERIOR DMN subnetwork abnormality PERSISTED in recovered patients, flagged as a residual biomarker and relapse-potential marker. This is direct evidence that the depressive network regime is partially -- but locus-specifically -- reversible: some sub-regimes reconfigure, one resists. Maps cleanly onto Q-061's framing that repair machinery reconfigures part of the regime while a residual locus persists.
failure_signatures: Anterior DMN hyperconnectivity persisted in clinically-recovered patients -- a 'reversible software state' reading of depression is falsified for at least one subnetwork even after symptomatic recovery.
Persistence of the anterior abnormality in asymptomatic patients indicates a reconfiguration that does not require full normalisation, complicating any single reversibility threshold.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Both anterior and posterior DMN subnetworks are hyperconnected in untreated MDD; after antidepressant treatment the posterior subnetwork normalises while the anterior subnetwork abnormality persists in recovered patients, serving as a candidate biomarker of asymptomatic depression and relapse risk.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports a PARTIAL-reversibility model of MECH-367's depressive network regime: REE's repair machinery (offline integration / MECH-124 replay rebalancing, decommitment, social re-access) would be expected to reconfigure some sub-regimes (cf. posterior normalisation) while a residual locked locus (cf. persistent anterior subnetwork) resists and underpins relapse -- consistent with neither full reversibility nor full chronicity-lock.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a 12-week treatment study in patients of mixed (not specifically >24-month chronic) illness duration, so it speaks to partial reversibility but does NOT directly test the RA-001 duration-threshold hypothesis (do early-effective routes fail late?). Human DMN connectivity is only a coarse analogue of REE's MECH-367 regime vector.
mapping.source_context: Human resting-state fMRI; 24 MDD patients, 29 controls; 18 patients re-scanned after 12 weeks of antidepressants; ICA-based DMN subnetwork decomposition (Friston co-author).

confidence_components.notes: Biol Psychiatry, longitudinal within-subject design; modest sample. Mapping fidelity is the highest of the Q-061 set because the anterior/posterior dissociation directly instantiates 'some repair routes work, one regime resists.'
